arxiv-1902-02132.title: The ℱ A \mathcal{F}^{A} Quantifier Fuzzification Mechanism: analysis of convergence and efficient implementations.
arxiv-1902-02132.creator: Félix Díaz-Hermida, Marcos Matabuena, Juan C. Vidal
arxiv-1902-02132.description: Abstract The fuzzy quantification model ℱ A \mathcal{F}^{A} has been identified as one of the best behaved quantification models in several revisions of the field of fuzzy quantification. This model is, to our knowledge, the unique one fulfilling the strict Determiner Fuzzification Scheme axiomatic framework that does not induce the standard min and max operators.

arxiv-2103-07698.description: Abstract We show that the most standard Eisenstein series such as E 4 ​ ( τ ) E_{4}(\tau) or 2 ​ E 2 ​ ( 2 ​ τ ) − E 2 ​ ( τ ) 2E_{2}(2\tau)-E_{2}(\tau) , and also the function θ 2 ​ ( τ ) \theta^{2}(\tau) , are in a natural way the product of two conjugate

arxiv-2104-09215.title: On the Correspondence between Nested Calculi and Semantic Systems for Intuitionistic Logics
arxiv-2104-09215.creator: Tim Lyon
arxiv-2104-09215.description: Abstract This paper studies the relationship between labelled and nested calculi for propositional intuitionistic logic, first-order intuitionistic logic with non-constant domains, and first-order intuitionistic logic with constant domains. It is shown that Fitting’s nested calculi naturally arise from their corresponding labelled calculi—for each of the aforementioned logics—via the elimination of structural rules in labelled derivations.

arxiv-2301-00048.title: Robustness of Variational Quantum Algorithms against stochastic parameter perturbation
arxiv-2301-00048.creator: Daniil Rabinovich, Ernesto Campos, Soumik Adhikary, Ekaterina Pankovets, Dmitry Vinichenko, Jacob Biamonte
arxiv-2301-00048.description: Abstract Variational quantum algorithms are tailored to perform within the constraints of current quantum devices, yet they are limited by performance-degrading errors. In this study, we consider a noise model that reflects realistic gate errors inherent to variational quantum algorithms.

arxiv-2409-15269.title: ReLoo: Reconstructing Humans Dressed in Loose Garments from Monocular Video in the Wild
arxiv-2409-15269.creator: Chen Guo, Tianjian Jiang, Manuel Kaufmann, Chengwei Zheng, Julien Valentin, Jie Song, Otmar Hilliges
arxiv-2409-15269.description: Abstract While previous years have seen great progress in the 3D reconstruction of humans from monocular videos, few of the state-of-the-art methods are able to handle loose garments that exhibit large non-rigid surface deformations during articulation. This limits the application of such methods to humans that are dressed in standard pants or T-shirts.

arxiv-2501-01382.title: BundleFit: Display and See-Through Models for Augmented Reality Head-Mounted Displays
arxiv-2501-01382.creator: Yufeng Zhu
arxiv-2501-01382.description: Abstract The head-mounted display is a vital component of augmented reality, incorporating optics with complex display and see-through optical behavior. Computationally modeling these optical behaviors requires meeting three key criteria: accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility. In recent years, various approaches have been proposed to model display and see-through optics, which can broadly be classified into black-box and white-box models.

arxiv-2502-04827.title: Uplink Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for Mobile Edge Computing with Short-Packet Communications Thanks: J. Xu is with Imperial College London. B. Clerckx is with the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Imperial College London, London SW7 2AZ, UK. (email: j.xu20,b.clerckx@imperial
arxiv-2502-04827.creator: Jiawei Xu, Yumeng Zhang, Yunnuo Xu, Bruno Clerckx
arxiv-2502-04827.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jiawei Xu, Yumeng Zhang, Yunnuo Xu, Bruno Clerckx. In this paper, a Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) scheme is proposed to assist a Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) system where local computation tasks from two users are offloaded to the MEC server, facilitated by uplink RSMA for processing. The efficiency of the MEC service is hence primarily influenced by the RSMA-aided task offloading phase and the subsequent task computation phase, where reliable and low-latency communication is required.

arxiv-2505-19963.title: Light propagation in the 2PN approximation in the monopole and quadrupole field of a body at rest: Boundary value problem
arxiv-2505-19963.creator: Sven Zschocke
arxiv-2505-19963.description: Abstract In a recent investigation, the initial value problem of light propagation in the gravitational field of a body at rest with monopole and quadrupole structure has been determined in the second post-Newtonian (2PN) approximation. In reality, the light source as well as the observer are located at finite distances from the solar system bodies.

pmc-10696825.title: De novo normotensive scleroderma renal crisis six years after living-donor renal transplantation in a patient with overlapping systemic sclerosis/systemic lupus erythematosus syndrome: a case report
pmc-10696825.creator: Hajime Sanada, Satoshi Hara, Makoto Horita, Hiroyuki Kawahara, Misaki Yoshida, Yoshinori Takahashi, Shunsuke Tsuge, Takeshi Zoshima, Ryo Nishioka, Kiyoaki Ito, Ichiro Mizushima, Takashi Matsushita, Mitsuhiro Kawano
pmc-10696825.description: BackgroundScleroderma renal crisis (SRC) is a critical kidney involvement of systemic sclerosis (SSc), often resulting in end-stage renal disease. Although the recurrence of SRC in the allograft has been reported, the development of de novo SRC after kidney transplantation has not been reported. Furthermore, normotensive SRC, which rarely occurs, makes prompt diagnosis more challenging.

pmc-10772943.title: Trichinella spp. detection in hunted wild boar (Sus scrofa) diaphragm biopsies in Central Italy
pmc-10772943.creator: Andrea Piccinini, Daniela Ronconi, Assunta De Luca, Valentina D’Ovidio, Gianluigi Ferri, Alberto Vergara
pmc-10772943.description: Trichinellosis is a globally diffused foodborne parasitic disease caused by nematodes of the Trichinella complex. During evolution, guided by ecological interactions, natural selection, and biochemical “intelligence”, these parasites developed admirable strategies to infect the host’s organism. One of the most fascinating is represented by the nurse cell formation in muscular tissue (e.g., diaphragm, skeletal muscle, extrinsic ocular muscles, etc.).

pmc-11381878.title: Isolation and identification of non-tuberculous mycobacteria from aquarium fish in Ilam, Iran
pmc-11381878.creator: Mohammad Yazdanmanesh, Keyvan Tadayon, Darya Bagherian Koshkghazi, Nader Mosavari
pmc-11381878.description: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are among the most important pathogens in wild, captive, marine, and freshwater fish species. So, it is important to consider fish as the primary source of infection for aquarium fish and humans. The present study analyzed the occurrence of NTM in aquarium fish in Ilam, west of Iran.

pmc-11481765.title: Diabetes knowledge, health literacy and diabetes self-care among older adults living with diabetes in Alexandria, Egypt
pmc-11481765.creator: Soha Magdy Ahmed Abdallah, Abla Ibrahim Ayoub, Mohamed Mohei Eldin Makhlouf, Ayat Ashour
pmc-11481765.description: BackgroundType 2 diabetes is a rising health problem, especially in older adults. Health literacy and the degree of diabetes knowledge are among the factors that may influence diabetes self-care activities. The aim of this study was to assess factors affecting self-care activities among older adults living with type 2 diabetes in Alexandria, Egypt.

pmc-11653940.title: Morel‐Lavallée Lesion: An Easily Missed Closed Debridement Injury in Blunt Trauma
pmc-11653940.creator: Hidetaka Mochizuki, Hirohito Hirata, Tomohito Yoshihara, Takaomi Kobayashi, Masatsugu Tsukamoto, Tetsuji Uemura, Masaaki Mawatari, Tadatsugu Morimoto
pmc-11653940.description: Morel‐Lavallée lesion (MLL) is a closed soft tissue injury following trauma that is often missed. If not treated appropriately, they can lead to infection and is difficult to treat. High‐energy trauma with shear forces should be treated with MLL in mind.

pmc-11711369.title: Exploring the Relationship Between YAP (Yes-Associated Protein) and VEGF-A with Distant Metastasis in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
pmc-11711369.creator: Lisnawati Rachmadi, Michelle Linggodigdo, Firman Hasan, Rahmat Cahyanur, Thariqah Salamah, Yayi Dwina Billianti Susanto
pmc-11711369.description: Objective:To investigate the relationship between Yes-Associated Protein (YAP) and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-A (VEGF-A) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and evaluate their potential as predictive biomarkers for distant metastasis. Methods:This observational analytic study was conducted from May to August 2023, including 60 NPC cases diagnosed histopathologically at the Department of Anatomical Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Indonesia/Cipto Mangunkusumo Hospital.

pmc-11716283.title: Identifying common disease trajectories of Alzheimer’s disease with electronic health records
pmc-11716283.creator: Mingzhou Fu, Timothy S Chang, UCLA Precision Health Data Discovery Repository Working Group
pmc-11716283.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD), a leading cause of dementia, poses a growing global public health challenge. While recent studies have identified AD risk factors, they often focus on specific comorbidities, neglecting the complex interrelations and temporal dynamics. Our study addresses this by analyzing AD progression through longitudinal trajectories, utilizing clinical diagnoses over time.

pmc-11864733.title: Lesion Volume as a Predictor for Return to Work After Endovascular Treatment: A 4‐Year Prospective Cohort Study
pmc-11864733.creator: Gisle Berg Helland, Mona Kristiansen Beyer, Brian Anthony B. Enriquez, Hege Ihle‐Hansen, Håkon Ihle‐Hansen, Stein Andersson, Esten Høyland Leonardsen, Helle Stangeland, Bettina Ùjhelyi, Guri Hagberg, Hanne Flinstad Harbo, Anne Hege Aamodt, Einar August Høgestøl
pmc-11864733.description: BackgroundThere are no known objective biomarkers for predicting return to work (RTW) in ischemic stroke survivors. This study aims to explore the predictive utility and defines a cutoff value of lesion volume on RTW after endovascular treatment.MethodsWe included patients aged <65 years undergoing endovascular treatment at Oslo University Hospital between January 2017 and May 2019.

pmc-12462941.title: Lipid‐Based Nanoparticles in Cancer Therapy: Advances in Targeted Drug Delivery and Therapeutic Potential for Renal Cell Carcinoma
pmc-12462941.creator: Wei Yao, Yuhe Lin, Yang Weng, Yan Wu, Lufeng Zheng, Donghan Zheng, Qi Xi, Jingying Zhao
pmc-12462941.description: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) remains a significant clinical challenge due to delayed diagnosis and multidrug resistance, necessitating innovative strategies to enhance early detection and therapeutic efficacy. This review evaluates the role of lipid‐based nanoparticles (LNPs), including liposomes, micelles, nanoemulsions, solid lipid nanoparticles, and nanostructured lipid carriers, as advanced drug delivery systems in providing innovative solutions for RCC diagnosis and treatment.

pmc-12538794.title: The association between the aggregate index of systemic inflammation and abdominal aortic calcification: a National health and nutrition examination survey
pmc-12538794.creator: Youfu Wang, Yiming Su, Changzhi Luo, Wenhong Jiang, Han Yang, Xiao Qin
pmc-12538794.description: BackgroundThe occurrence of abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) is associated with inflammation. This study aims to explore the relationship between the aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI) and AAC.MethodsWe utilized data from the 2013–2014 cycle of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A loge transformation was applied to AISI (logeAISI) to preserve its normal distribution.

pmc-12562876.title: Glycan Signatures on Neutrophils in an Equine Model for Autoimmune Uveitis
pmc-12562876.creator: Carolin J Sprenzel, Barbara Amann, Cornelia A Deeg, Roxane L Degroote, Myron R Szewczuk
pmc-12562876.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Glycosylation of surface proteins is a crucial post-translational modification that reflects the activation status of neutrophils, the predominant leukocyte subset in humans and horses. Neutrophils have emerged as active contributors to diseases mediated by the adaptive immune system, such as equine recurrent uveitis (ERU), a sight-threatening disease in horses and a unique model for studying the pathogenesis of autoimmune uveitis in humans.

pmc-12579937.title: Exploring potential salivary biomarkers for dental caries: a systematic review
pmc-12579937.creator: Mónica López-Galindo, William Atashkadeh
pmc-12579937.description: Background Dental caries remains one of the most widespread non-communicable diseases. Saliva is crucial for maintaining oral health as it shields teeth from demineralization and promotes the remineralization of enamel. Although ongoing studies are investigating the relationship between various salivary proteins and dental caries, consensus in existing literature has not yet been established.

pmc-12972639.title: Langat Virus Biology and Infection
pmc-12972639.creator: Zinaida Klestova, Daniel Sauter, Michael Schindler, Thomas Iftner
pmc-12972639.description: Flaviviruses pose a major threat to global health and can cause severe disease in animals and humans. Among them, tick‐borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) and related members of the tick‐borne encephalitis (TBE) serocomplex are transmitted primarily by ticks and can lead to neurological disease, including encephalitis and death.

pmc-13203280.title: Protective Effects of Recombinant Lactobacillus paracasei Expressing Porcine β-Defensin 2 Against DSS-Induced Colitis in a Murine Model
pmc-13203280.creator: Ying Chen, Zhixuan Guo, Fangjie Yin, Yiting Guo, Jiaxuan Li, Xiaona Wang
pmc-13203280.description: Simple SummaryInflammatory bowel diseases are a major challenge in both human and animal medicine, necessitating the development of safe and effective biological treatments. This study engineered a probiotic strain, Lactobacillus paracasei, to produce and secrete a natural defense protein called porcine β-defensin 2 (pBD2).

pmc-13253771.title: Vessel diameter as a potential predictor of pulsed dye laser response in port wine stain: a retrospective exploratory reflectance confocal microscopy study
pmc-13253771.creator: Xuehui Ran, Ying Shang, Xia Yang, Yufeng Wang, Hao Peng, Lingyue Shen

pmc-13437906.title: Molecular modulators of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitor response in experimental glioma identified through genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening
pmc-13437906.creator: Surender Surender, Lara Annina Haeusser, Laurence Kuhlburger, Foteini Tsiami, Nihal Olcay Dogan, Louise Maise, Sven Nahnsen, Susanne Beck, Daniel Josef Merk, Ghazaleh Tabatabai

pmc-13485396.title: Validation of the Chinese Stress Sensitivity Inventory and Its Association With Internet Gaming Disorder Symptoms
pmc-13485396.creator: Yanyin Zhou, Yi Wang, Yunjie Du, Xiaoyuan Liao, Yuanfeng Wang, Xiaohong Peng, Yu Huang, Kezhi Liu, Ke Gong, Min Liang, Jing Chen, Wei Lei
pmc-13485396.description: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Chinese version of the Stress Sensitivity Inventory (SSI), a self-reported instrument that assesses trait stress sensitivity in adults, and to examine the relationship between the SSI and symptoms of internet gaming disorder (IGD).

pmc-13575723.title: How do supermarkets shape the experience of vulnerable people in Australia's food system? A scoping review
pmc-13575723.creator: Casey E. Webb, Jeremy Farr, Nathan Cook, Olivia R. L. Wright
pmc-13575723.description: AimsThe aim of this scoping review was to synthesise how supermarkets shape health behaviours and nutrition‐related outcomes of vulnerable populations in Australia.MethodsFive databases were searched and studies were included if they discussed Australia's major supermarket chains, their relationship with vulnerable populations, and outcomes linked to nutrition behaviour or health.

pmc-13676143.title: Azithromycin in crisis: antimicrobial resistance, diagnostics gaps, and vaccine-linked stewardship for enteric infections in low- and middle-income countries
pmc-13676143.creator: Jobin John Jacob, Madhumathi Irulappan, Kamini Walia, Yamuna Devi Bakthavatchalam, Balaji Veeraraghavan
pmc-13676143.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Azithromycin resistance is rising among major enteric pathogens in low- and middle-income countries.•Mechanisms and clinical impact vary across Shigella, Salmonella, and Campylobacter.•Diagnostics and pathogen-directed stewardship are critical interventions.•Surveillance is key to preserving azithromycin efficacy.Keywords: Azithromycin, S. Paratyphi, Shigella sp, Non-typhoidal Salmonella, Campylobacter Introduction Azithromycin has become one of the most commonly prescribed oral agents for bacterial enteric infections, largely driven by increasing fluoroquinolone resistance and the need for effective outpatient antimicrobial therapy.
